original_problem.title: E2
original_problem.description:
The only difference with E1 is the question of the problem.

Vlad built a maze out of $n$ rooms and $n-1$ bidirectional corridors. From any room $u$ any other room $v$ can be reached through a sequence of corridors. Thus, the room system forms an undirected tree.

Vlad invited $k$ friends to play a game with them.

Vlad starts the game in the room $1$ and wins if he reaches a room other than $1$, into which exactly one corridor leads. Friends are placed in the maze: the friend with number $i$ is in the room $x_i$, and no two friends are in the same room (that is, $x_i \neq x_j$ for all $i \neq j$). Friends win if one of them meets Vlad in any room or corridor before he wins.

For one unit of time, each participant of the game can go through one corridor. All participants move at the same time. Participants may not move. Each room can fit all participants at the same time.

Friends know the plan of a maze and intend to win. They don't want to waste too much energy. They ask you to determine if they can win and if they can, what minimum number of friends must remain in the maze so that they can always catch Vlad.

In other words, you need to determine the size of the minimum (by the number of elements) subset of friends who can catch Vlad or say that such a subset does not exist.


-----Input-----

The first line of the input contains an integer $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$) — the number of test cases in the input. The input contains an empty string before each test case.

The first line of the test case contains two numbers $n$ and $k$ ($1 \le k < n \le 2\cdot 10^5$) — the number of rooms and friends, respectively.

The next line of the test case contains $k$ integers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_k$ ($2 \le x_i \le n$) — numbers of rooms with friends. All $x_i$ are different.

The next $n-1$ lines contain descriptions of the corridors, two numbers per line $v_j$ and $u_j$ ($1 \le u_j, v_j \le n$) — numbers of rooms that connect the $j$ corridor. All corridors are bidirectional. From any room, you can go to any other by moving along the corridors.

It is guaranteed that the sum of the values $n$ over all test cases in the test is not greater than $2\cdot10^5$.


-----Output-----

Print $t$ lines, each line containing the answer to the corresponding test case. The answer to a test case should be $-1$ if Vlad wins anyway and a minimal number of friends otherwise.


-----Examples-----

Input
4

8 2
5 3
4 7
2 5
1 6
3 6
7 2
1 7
6 8

8 4
6 5 7 3
4 7
2 5
1 6
3 6
7 2
1 7
6 8

3 1
2
1 2
2 3

3 2
2 3
3 1
1 2
Output
-1
2
1
2


-----Note-----

In the first set of inputs, even if all the friends stay in the maze, Vlad can still win. Therefore, the answer is "-1".

In the second set of inputs it is enough to leave friends from rooms $6$ and $7$. Then Vlad will not be able to win. The answer is "2".

In the third and fourth sets of inputs Vlad cannot win only if all his friends stay in the maze. Therefore the answers are "1" and "2".

1

components.role_description: the number of rooms and the number of marked rooms (friends/tags)
initial positions of the friends (tags placed in rooms)
desired minimum number of friends required to capture the opponent; -1 means Vlad always wins despite any friend arrangement

constraints.name: tree_structure
constraints.description: The rooms and corridors form an undirected tree: n nodes, n-1 edges, connected, no cycles.
constraints.formal: G = (V, E) is a tree, |V| = n, |E| = n-1, connected.

constraints.name: vlad_win_condition
constraints.description: Vlad starts in room 1 and wins if he reaches a room other than 1 that has degree 1 (a leaf).

constraints.name: friends_initial_positions
constraints.description: There are k friends placed in distinct rooms with indices between 2 and n; no two friends occupy the same room.
constraints.formal: Positions {x_i} ⊂ {2, 3, ..., n}, x_i ≠ x_j for i ≠ j.

constraints.name: simultaneous_movement
constraints.description: All participants move at the same time; each can move along at most one corridor per unit of time or stay in the current room.
constraints.formal: ∀ player, at each step: move to adjacent node or stay.

constraints.name: capture_condition
constraints.description: Friends win if one of them meets Vlad in any room or corridor before Vlad reaches a winning room; otherwise Vlad wins.
constraints.formal: Capture if ∃ t < T_win, friend and Vlad share a node or traverse the same edge (in opposite directions or simultaneously).

constraints.name: target_binding
constraints.description: The provided target_min_friends value must equal the minimum required friend subset size (or -1 if impossible) for the game on the tree after all modifications are applied.
constraints.formal: Let G' be the tree after edge edits. Let f(G') be the minimum number of friends from the original set needed to guarantee capture (or -1). The condition is: f(G') = target_min_friends.

constraints.name: edit_operations
constraints.description: Allowed modifications: Only add or delete edges between rooms. The graph must remain a tree at every intermediate step and in the final state. No changes to friend positions or the number of rooms are allowed.
constraints.formal: An edit operation is a tuple (u, v) ∈ V×V, u≠v. If {u,v} ∈ E, remove it; if {u,v} ∉ E, add it. After each operation, the graph must be a tree (|E| = n-1, connected, acyclic).

constraints.name: minimality_obligation
constraints.description: The output must be a sequence of edit operations of minimum length that achieves the target condition, or state impossibility if no such sequence exists.
constraints.formal: Output an integer L (minimum number of edits) and optionally the sequence, or -1 if impossible. Any correct solution must provide a proof of minimality (e.g., lower bound argument).

objective.description: Minimize the number of edge additions or deletions required to transform the tree so that the minimum required number of friends equals target_min_friends.

invariants.name: tree_structure_invariance
invariants.description: Throughout the editing process, the graph must remain a tree. That is, it is always connected and acyclic, with exactly n-1 edges.

invariants.name: target_achievability
invariants.description: For any sequence of valid edits leading to a tree, the minimum friend set size is well-defined and can be compared to target_min_friends. This property ensures the problem is decidable.

invariants.name: minimality_certificate
invariants.description: A solution claiming optimality must supply a certificate (e.g., an argument that any fewer edits cannot achieve the target) that proves the output edit count is minimal.

generated_problem.title: 收纳柜的改造
generated_problem.description:
小明的家里有一个巨大的收纳柜，柜子由 n 个格子组成，格子之间通过 n−1 条通道连接，任意两个格子都可以互相到达，因此整个通道结构形成一棵树。小明很喜欢玩捉迷藏，他每次都从 1 号格子出发，目标是到达一个只连有一条通道的尽头格子（1 号格子本身不算）。

为了阻止小明，家长们在某些格子上放置了标签。所有标签的位置互不相同，并且不会放在 1 号格子。游戏开始时，小明和所有标签同时行动。每单位时间，每位参与者可以选择沿着一条通道移动到相邻格子，也可以留在原地。如果某个标签和小明在某一时刻出现在同一格子或者同一条通道上（包括迎面相遇或擦肩而过），则标签成功抓住了小明。

家长们希望用最少的标签来保证一定能抓住小明。也就是说，对于给定的标签集合，他们想知道：最少需要保留其中的几个标签，才能无论小明怎么走，都必然在到达尽头格子之前被抓住？如果即使保留全部标签，小明仍然有办法获胜，则记这个最少数量为 −1。

现在，你已经知道所有标签的初始位置，还知道一个目标值 K（K 可以是 −1，或者一个正整数）。你可以对柜子的通道进行一次“整理”：每次整理时，选择一条当前存在的通道并将其封住，同时在另一对目前没有直接相连的格子之间开辟一条新的通道。整理完毕后，整个柜子的通道结构必须仍然是一棵树（即没有环且所有格子连通）。

你的任务是：通过若干次这样的整理，使得整理后，所需的最少标签数量恰好等于 K。你需要求出达到这一目标所需的最小整理次数。如果无论怎样整理都无法满足要求，则输出 −1。
generated_problem.input_format:
第一行一个整数 t (1≤t≤10^4)，表示测试数据组数。
接下来是 t 组测试数据，每组数据的格式如下：
第一行两个整数 n,m (2≤n≤2⋅10^5, 1≤m<n)，分别表示格子数和标签数。
第二行 m 个互不相同的整数 x1,x2,…,xm (2≤xi≤n)，表示标签所在的格子编号。
第三行一个整数 K (−1≤K≤m)，表示目标最少标签数。若 K=−1，表示希望小明总能获胜；否则 K 是一个非负整数，且保证 0≤K≤m，但注意 K=0 在实际中不可能达到，因为至少需要一个标签才能保证抓住小明。
接下来 n−1 行，每行两个整数 u,v (1≤u,v≤n)，表示一条通道连接格 u 和格 v。保证给出的图是一棵树。

保证所有测试数据的 n 之和不超过 2⋅10^5。
generated_problem.output_format: 对每组测试数据，输出一行一个整数，表示所需的最少整理次数。如果无法达到目标，输出 −1。

samples.explanation:
初始树中，小明从 1 出发，第一步只能走到 2。标签在 2 和 3。若只保留标签 2，小明走到 2 时会被抓住；若只保留标签 3，标签 3 也可以从 3 移动到 2 抓住小明（根据同时移动规则）。因此只需要 1 个标签即可保证抓住小明。目标 K=2 要求最少标签数为 2。
进行一次整理：封住通道 (2,3)，同时开辟通道 (1,3)。新树为 1−2, 1−3, 3−4。此时小明从 1 出发可以选择走向 2 或 3。若只有标签 2，小明可以走 3→4 到达尽头格子 4 而获胜；若只有标签 3，小明可以走 2 到达尽头格子 2 而获胜。因此必须同时保留标签 2 和标签 3 才能保证抓住小明，最少标签数为 2，恰好满足目标。故最少整理次数为 1。
初始树中，小明从 1 出发，可以走 1→3→4 到达尽头格子 4，而唯一的标签在 2。标签从 2 移动到 3 或 4 的速度无法快于小明，小明总是能获胜。因此即使保留所有标签也无法抓住小明，最少标签数为 −1，恰好等于目标 K=−1，无需整理。
只有一个标签，而目标 K=2 要求最少需要 2 个标签。由于整理不能增加标签数量，不可能达到目标，故输出 −1。

generated_problem.notes: 每次整理操作定义为：选择一条当前存在的通道并删除，同时选择一对当前没有直接通道的格子并建立新通道，操作后整个图必须仍是一棵树。如果目标 K 大于标签数 m，显然不可能实现，此时应输出 −1。当 K=−1 时，表示希望小明总能获胜，即任何标签子集都不能保证必定抓住小明。对于 K 的其他取值，保证 K 不超过 m。

algorithmic_delta_claim.seed_solver_core: BFS simulation to compute the minimal set of friends that can intercept Vlad, effectively simulating wavefront expansion from friends and Vlad simultaneously.
algorithmic_delta_claim.reusable_subroutines: The BFS simulator that, given a tree and friend positions, returns the minimal required friends count or -1. This can be used as an oracle to evaluate a candidate modified tree.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_solver_core: A search on the space of edge modifications, possibly using iterative deepening or BFS on the graph of trees, or a more specialized algorithm that exploits structural monotonicity (e.g., adding edges can only reduce minimal friends, deleting edges can only increase it) to compute the minimum edit distance. Alternatively, formulate as a shortest path in the tree edit space with pruning using the oracle.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_proof_obligation: Must prove monotonicity of the minimum friend set size under edge modifications (e.g., deleting an edge never decreases the required number, adding never increases it). Then design an algorithm that uses this property to efficiently search for the minimum edits, and prove its correctness and optimality. Also, need to prove that the oracle (reused subroutine) correctly computes the value for any tree.
algorithmic_delta_claim.why_direct_reuse_fails: Direct reuse of the original solution only evaluates a single fixed tree; it cannot explore the space of possible trees or guarantee that a minimal sequence of edits is found. A new search framework and optimality proofs are mandatory.

review_context.anti_shallow_rationale: 本题不是简单更换背景或参数，而是从正向求解翻转为反向设计，引入了结构修改操作和目标满足性约束，求解方向从计算答案变为最小化编辑代价，需要全新的算法和证明义务。
